releases.title: Laughs come through
items: A loud laugh, a shout or singing no longer gets eaten by Noise suppression.

releases.title: Quieter when you're muted
items: Talking while muted blips only the first time after you mute; after that "You're muted" shows by the button without a sound.
No "You're muted" reminder while another of your devices is unmuted in the same call.

releases.title: Links to every place
items: Desktop app: right-click a text channel or a place (Draw, Space, Watch, When's good, the board) and pick Copy link to send friends straight there; the title bar's link button copies one to what's open.
Every place (Draw, Space, Watch, When's good, the board) and text channel has its own link: the button next to its name copies it, and anyone here who opens it lands right there.
Desktop app: a link in a message to a channel, a message or a place on your server (Draw, Space, Watch, When's good, the board) now takes you there.
iPhone and Mac: Copy link on a text channel or a place (long-press or right-click it, or its "…" menu) gives a link that takes anyone here straight there.
iPhone and Mac: tapping a link to a place or channel on your server opens it right in the app.

releases.title: Safer sign-ins and sturdier apps
items: Desktop app: changing your password says it signs out your other devices, and how many it did.
iPhone and Mac: changing your password says your other devices will be signed out, and how many were.
iPhone and Mac: Settings › Owner & mods shows when someone changed their name, from what to what.
Desktop app: a broken or booby-trapped soundboard clip or join chime can no longer crash the app.
Desktop app: oversized or booby-trapped pictures, GIFs and shared screens can no longer crash the app or eat all its memory.
Desktop app: updates are now signed for their exact version and platform, so an older or wrong build can never be installed as an update.
Desktop app: plain http:// server addresses are refused (except for a server on your own computer), so your invite key and password never travel unencrypted.
Desktop app: on Linux, notifications show a member's text as text, never as formatting or links.
Desktop app: with Hide my IP on, a call never connects directly any more: without the server's voice relay it says so instead, and the setting can always be turned off.
Changing your password now signs out your other devices and OBS links, and a password reset by the owner or a mod signs out all of that person's devices.
Nobody can take a name that looks just like someone else's (other capitals, accents or look-alike letters from another alphabet), and name changes show in the mod log.
Pictures can be up to 8192 pixels a side (animations 4096), and each person can upload up to 300 MB a day.
Soundboard clips and join chimes are stored exactly as they were measured, so they sound the same in every app.
A sign-in link opened in a browser now asks "Signed in as … Is that you?" first, and Add to Home Screen's sign-in link lasts 5 minutes.
OBS links no longer contain the invite link, and can play everyone but you; the default plays everyone, you too (talk on your phone, record the game on your PC).
Hide my IP never falls back to a direct connection: with no voice relay, it says so instead.
Desktop app: a malformed voice or screen-share packet from someone in a call can no longer crash or freeze the app.
Desktop app: a message or plan with an impossible date can no longer crash the app.
Desktop app: a malformed drawing on the Draw board can no longer freeze the app.
Desktop app: a broken Personal space key from the server can no longer keep the app busy for hours.
iPhone and Mac: a malformed voice message from someone in a call can no longer crash the app, and neither can odd numbers, sound clips or oversized avatars and emoji from the server.
iPhone and Mac: an invite link starting with http:// is refused (unless it's a test server on the same computer), so your password never crosses the network unencrypted.
iPhone and Mac: signing out also signs Draw, Space and the board out, so the next person on a shared iPad or Mac doesn't open them as you.
iPhone and Mac: a link to another site in Draw, Space or the board opens in your browser instead of inside Yap.
iPhone and Mac: signed out from another device (or by a new password), the app goes straight to the sign-in screen instead of trying to reconnect first.
iPhone and Mac: with Hide my IP address on and no voice relay on the server, calls never connect directly: the call says you can't reach anyone, and the setting can always be turned off.
iPhone and Mac: Full res pictures stay within 8192 pixels a side and 40 megapixels (bigger ones go a little smaller).
Desktop app: a message claiming an impossible picture size can no longer break the chat's layout.
Custom emojis and avatars can be up to 2048 pixels a side.

releases.title: Drafts, Rejoin, Mic volume and a steadier Yap
items: Watch together: removing a video from the queue always takes out the one you clicked, even if the queue moved up a moment before.
Settings › Voice › Mic volume makes you louder or quieter for everyone (0–200 %), live while you drag; past 100 % a soft limiter rounds off your loudest moments so they don't clip.
After a reload or a crash in a call, a bar says "You were in Lounge." with a Rejoin button that puts you straight back in.
Tapping a push about a message (an @mention, a reply) opens Yap at that message.
Each channel keeps what you'd typed in it: switch away and back and your draft is still there (and Enter never sends it to the wrong channel).
Scrolled up reading? A "↓ New messages" pill says when something new arrives below, and takes you there.
Installed as an app, Yap's icon shows how many @mentions are waiting for you.
Desktop app: Settings › Voice › Mic volume (0–200 %) turns how loud you come across up or down.
Desktop app: if Yap restarts while you're in a call (an update, a crash), it offers "You were in Lounge. Rejoin" for 10 minutes.
Desktop app: a "↓ New messages" button shows when someone writes while you're scrolled up.
Desktop app: a picture waiting to be sent stays with the channel you picked it in.
Desktop app: an @mention while Yap is in the background flashes its taskbar button (Windows) or bounces its Dock icon (Mac), and the Dock shows how many are unread.
iPhone and Mac: what you typed in a channel waits there while you look at another one.
iPhone and Mac: scrolled up when someone writes? A "New messages" button takes you down.
iPhone and Mac: your unread @mentions show on the app icon (and the Mac's Dock).
iPhone and Mac: tapping an @mention's notification opens that message.
iPhone and Mac: after Yap restarts mid-call, "You were in Lounge." offers to rejoin.

iPhone and Mac: Settings › Voice › Mic volume sets your mic's own level (0–100 %), where the mic lets Yap set it. On a Mac that's the same level as System Settings › Sound › Input, so it changes it for every app.
Desktop app: when the network swallows the connection, it says "The server didn't answer in time" after 15 s and keeps trying, instead of "Connecting…" for ever.
Desktop app: a message it doesn't understand (from a newer server, say) with an emoji or accented letter in it no longer crashes the app every time it connects.
Desktop app: pasting an invite link with a stray "%" can no longer crash the app.
Desktop app: pictures and emojis that didn't load (say, right after waking from sleep) load by themselves a moment later, and a screenful of emojis loads faster.
Desktop app: @mentions of someone who just changed their name show up as mentions.
Desktop app (Linux): notifications for messages that start with a dash show up.
iPhone and Mac: when the network drops while Yap is connecting, it tries again within seconds instead of a minute.
Scrolling far back in a long channel and the daily backup do much less work on the server.
The one-ping-a-minute limit now always holds.
Watch together: a slow YouTube holds up starting a video for 4 seconds at most (it then plays without its title).
After your phone wakes up or the network changes, Yap notices a dead connection within 10 seconds, and a connection attempt that hangs is retried after 15 seconds instead of a minute or more.
Jumping to a message no longer gets stuck if the connection drops while it loads.
Draw: a second finger on a phone or tablet no longer hijacks your stroke.
Draw: Clear no longer throws the page away when it can't be kept in the gallery, and Save only says "saved" when it was.
Draw: resizing the window with a busy page is instant.
Space: keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+Shift+D no longer move your character, and ⌘ no longer leaves you walking.
When's good: you can keep typing a hang's plan while friends paint their times.
If a picture fails to upload, it stays ready to send again, with its caption (it used to vanish).
Yap no longer restarts itself for an update while a picture is waiting to be sent or still uploading.
"Jump to first unread" appears as soon as the "New since" line scrolls out of view.
Clicking a browser notification for an @mention takes you to that message.
Locking your Personal space also closes the pictures it had opened.
Attaching pictures uses less memory, and the emoji picker opens a little faster.
The board: your pointer no longer lingers at the edge for others after you move off it.
Watch together: on a slow connection the video plays (a little behind) instead of jumping back and forth.
Watch together: a video YouTube won't play here no longer asks you to "Click to join the show".
iPhone: after a call, Yap's sounds no longer stop your music or ignore the silent switch.
Desktop app: dropping a few files at once sends the picture among them, and dropping a huge file by mistake no longer freezes the window.
Doodle reactions: a second finger on the pad no longer scribbles into your line.
Space: after a reconnect or an update you show up on everyone's map straight away, not only once you move.
Changing a voice setting twice in a row (like Noise suppression) no longer leaves your first choice on.
Friends you've turned up past 100 % (or hear left and right in Space) now move to the speakers you pick, and come back after the system interrupts the sound.
Moving to another voice channel while sharing your screen shows it as LIVE there; moving away from a screen you're watching closes it.
When Yap takes you out of a voice channel (say it was archived), your screen share and soundboard clips stop too.
OBS overlay: the speaking glow now eases in and out instead of snapping.
iPhone and Mac: Yap stays light in long sessions with lots of pictures.
iPhone and Mac: a call whose channel is archived while you're reconnecting now ends cleanly, screen share included.
A message sent just as the connection dropped no longer shows up twice.

releases.title: A new icon
items: iPhone: Dictation, Siri or Control Center no longer drop you from a call; if the sound stops, Yap starts it again by itself.
iPhone: Tapping one of Yap's notifications no longer crashes the app.
iPhone: your voice call shows on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, with Mute, Deafen and a × to leave.
A new Yap icon: a cleaner pixel speech bubble on teal, everywhere (on iPhone it follows dark and tinted Home Screens too).

releases.title: Build on Yap
items: For people building on Yap: a "Build on Yap" guide and a tiny example client.

releases.title: MIT License
items: Yap is now under the MIT License.

releases.title: A simpler icon
items: A simpler Yap icon: the pixel speech bubble on teal, the same on the web, iPhone, Mac and desktop.

releases.title: Little things from Mumble
items: If you talk while muted, Yap reminds you with a soft blip and "You're muted" (at most every 5 s; you can turn it off in Settings › Voice).

Mute and deafen shortcuts (Ctrl/⌘+Shift+M and Ctrl/⌘+Shift+D), and push-to-mute: hold a key to cough. Desktop app: global keys for all three, and `yap --remote mute` for Stream Decks and Linux shortcuts.
Push-to-talk clicks when it opens and closes; double-tap it to stay live, tap again to stop.
If your connection is dropping some of your audio, Yap now tells you, not just the people who hear it; the call report shows how much each friend lost of yours.
Voice rows show the volume you set for someone (and a muted speaker at 0); Ctrl/⌘ + scroll over a name changes it.
An option to lower Watch together and screen-share sound while friends talk (Settings › Voice, off by default).
Space: voices come from the left or right, where people stand (web and desktop app).
The mic meter warns when you're too loud (clipping), and 256/510 kbps now say what they cost.
iPhone and Mac: someone's volume now really changes how loud they are for you (0 %, 50 % and the boost past 100 % never worked before).

releases.title: The OBS link, VDO.Ninja's way
items: The OBS link plays the call the way VDO.Ninja does: each voice straight through with nothing added while anyone talks, and it starts playing again by itself if it's paused.

releases.title: OBS link rollback
items: The OBS link no longer distorts the call: v0.45.0's lower-delay settings are undone while it's reworked.

releases.title: A cleaner OBS link
items: In OBS, the first words after a pause no longer come out cut or glitchy (OBS's browser stopped listening during silence; the OBS link now keeps it listening with an inaudible tone).
The OBS link plays the call with less delay: straight through, with the shortest buffer and smaller packets.

releases.title: Reset the main link
items: The owner can reset the main invite link (Settings › Invite, behind a warning), in every app. Everyone already signed in keeps working and gets the new link by itself; only people who haven't joined yet need the new one.
An OBS link only listens while you're in the call, or for 5 minutes after you leave. Meanwhile you show greyed out in the channel ("…'s OBS is still listening") so people know.
One Noise suppression switch, using the stronger filter (RNNoise) everywhere it can run.
Test mic in Settings › Voice now shows it's listening (the bar moves and the button says Stop test), works during a call, and says what's wrong when the mic can't be heard.

releases.title: Passwords instead of PINs
items: Yap uses passwords now (8 characters or more) instead of 6-digit PINs, in every app. Your PIN still works until you choose a password; Yap asks once, and a wrong sign-in reminds you an old PIN works there too.
Only the owner and mods let new people in from the waiting room, and they get a push when someone's waiting. Everyone still sees "Cleo joined — invited by Ada".
Owners and mods: Reset password… gives a temporary password to send; the person chooses their own after signing in.
Pings: one a minute per person.
An OBS link listens without showing up in the voice channel, in every app. Leave it in OBS: it keeps working until you turn it off.

releases.title: Calls that hold up
items: Calls hold up better on choppy Wi‑Fi and cellular, in every app: each bit of voice now travels twice, so a short dropout is filled with the real sound instead of a robotic blip.
Copy call report (in a call's ⋯ menu, or Settings › Voice afterwards) copies what Yap noticed about a call, so one that sounded off can be looked into. It stays on your device.
Sending lots of messages at once no longer leaves one stuck as "sending", in every app: it goes out a moment later.
Desktop app: echo cancellation, so friends no longer hear themselves when you use speakers instead of headphones.
Desktop app: on a Mac (macOS 14 or newer), Share screen uses Apple's own picker, so macOS stops asking again and again whether Yap may record your screen.
iPhone and Mac: calls no longer drop when your iPhone's screen is off: the call's sound keeps running the whole time, even when people come and go or the connection hiccups.

iPhone and Mac: if something still ends a call while Yap is in the background (a phone call takes the sound, the connection is gone for a minute), Yap tells you, "You left Lounge" and why, and one tap puts you back in.
iPhone and Mac: switching between Wi‑Fi and cellular reconnects right away.
iPhone and iPad: share your screen: Share screen in the call, then Start Broadcast. Friends click your LIVE badge to watch; stop it in Yap, in Control Center or with the red pill.
iPhone: Mic mode in Settings › Voice opens Apple's Voice Isolation, which cuts the noise around you.

releases.title: One look, and screen sharing in every app
items: One look: Windows 98, in light or dark. The Apple and Arch looks are gone; if you used one, Yap switches you over.
Screen sharing: see who's watching, switch quality, window or sound without stopping, and a bigger viewer with its own volume that tells you when a screen is paused or has stopped.
Screen sharing: the web can watch shares from the desktop and iPhone/Mac apps.
A screen share's sound follows the speakers you pick in Settings, like voices do.
Desktop app: share your screen and watch other people's right in the app, sound included.
Desktop app: on a Mac, sharing your screen uses the hardware video encoder, so it's lighter on the computer.
Desktop app: click or right-click someone in a voice channel for their volume, Watch screen and mod actions.
Desktop app: the same single look, Windows 98 in light or dark.
iPhone and Mac: watch someone's screen right in the app (tap LIVE; pop it out, go full screen, set its sound), and share your screen from the Mac, seeing who's watching.
iPhone and Mac: tap or right-click someone in a voice channel to change their volume or watch their screen.
iPhone and Mac: the same single look, Windows 98 in light or dark.

releases.title: Polish everywhere
items: Desktop app: in People, a long "invited by …" line under someone waiting now wraps instead of being cut off.
Desktop app: in the Arch skin, the pinned and waiting counts in the chat header no longer hide their buttons.
iPhone and Mac: after resetting someone's PIN, the temporary PIN shows in Yap's own box for your skin, with a Copy PIN button.
Arch skin: drop-down menus (microphone, notifications, away message…) show their little arrow again, so you can tell they open.
The reaction picker, doodle pad, soundboard and a person's volume menu open above what you clicked when there's no room below, instead of covering it.
Windows 98 skin: you can reach a message's buttons (reply, react, edit…) with the Tab key, and screen readers read them.
Windows 98 skin on phones: the little dot on the ☰ button (new messages or a mention elsewhere) sits on the button again instead of half off the screen.
Personal space on phones: the title is readable again ("Personal" instead of "P…") and the message box hint fits on one line.
iPhone and Mac: in the Windows 98 and Apple looks, people waiting to join now show as a bar above the chat with Let in and Turn away, like on the web.
Keyboard: you can reach people in a voice channel and in People with Tab (volume, mod tools), and the sidebar no longer loses your place when something changes.
Keyboard: sliders, switches and drop-down menus show a focus ring (or highlight) when you Tab onto them, in every skin.
Screen readers: dialogs say their names, a reaction says who reacted and whether yours is on.
iPhone and Mac: in the Arch look with very large text, the message box gets the whole width instead of a narrow strip.
Windows 98 skin: long messages that fold behind "Show more" no longer indent every line, and don't jump when you open them.
Arch skin: "Show more" under a long message lines up with the text.
Catch up on a phone says "Tap one…" instead of "Click one…".
Longer notices at the bottom of the screen use the full width on phones instead of a thin column (and in the Apple skin they're no longer a circle).
iPhone and Mac: questions use the same words as the web, and cancelling a hang asks first.
Esc closes the doodle pad and the soundboard too, and after closing any picker you're back in the message box (or on the button you came from).
A mistyped address shows a "Page not found" window with a way back to Yap instead of a blank page.
The OBS page now says where to get a new link: Settings › Voice › Advanced › Stream to OBS.
Signing in with a wrong PIN now tells you the owner or a mod can reset it if you forgot it.
Windows 98 dark: the × on the "easy to guess" PIN bar is visible again.
Draw: when the toolbar takes two rows, Undo, Save, GIF, Share and Clear stay on the right.
Draw: Clear's question shows its three buttons on one row.
Draw on phones: the gallery is a tidy grid of bigger thumbnails.
When's good on phones: best times no longer break in the middle, and planned hangs wrap cleanly.
Apple and Arch skins: the voice panel's "Voice connected" and "Reconnecting…" no longer run under the Share and Sounds buttons.
When's good: the "8 AM" label under the folded night hours is no longer half hidden.
When's good: the voice channel picker in "Plan a hang" looks like a dropdown in every skin (and Space's voice picker in Arch).
When's good (Apple, Arch): the time you tap is outlined even when everyone is free then.
Cancel works in "Change PIN or password" and in the Personal space passcode sheet (it used to complain and stay open).
Changing your PIN: a mistake is explained plainly ("Your new PIN is exactly 6 digits.") instead of the browser's "Please match the requested format".
Arch: Draw's and Space's buttons no longer zoom on hover; the picked brush, tool and layer get a thin accent border.
Windows 98 skin: writing a long message no longer stretches the Send, GIF and emoji buttons into tall slabs.
Space on phones: the room's "here · elsewhere" count no longer runs out of its box.
Space on phones: the Character picker opens above the button bar instead of covering it, and the bar fits the screen.
Screen readers: the channel list says which channels have new messages or mentions, who in a voice channel is muted, and Pictures & GIFs names each picture.
Space: a drawing you walk up to in the Gallery opens beside the room card instead of covering its wall buttons.
Apple on phones: Watch together's row of seats fits the screen.
Windows 98 on phones: places show their whole name in the title bar ("Watch together", not "Watch toge… - Yap").
Board: the names on other people's pointers match your skin (a yellow tooltip in Windows 98, flat and monospace in Arch).
Windows 98 skin: the small grey hints in Settings and other windows are easier to read, especially in the light theme.
iPhone and Mac: Settings › Owner & mods › Activity uses the same plain words as the web.
iPhone and Mac: a folded long message says how long it is ("Show more (3,440 characters)"), like on the web.
Watch together: the video's title lines up with "3 watching" and Leave.
Draw: pointing at a saved drawing shows who drew it and when, and screen readers read it out.
Signing in or up with a password: the hint above the form talks about your password, not a PIN.
iPhone and Mac: the new sign-in alert's buttons are no longer cut off in the Mac sidebar.
"Ping everyone?" explains what happens in plainer words (and the same ones the iPhone app uses).
iPhone and Mac: in the Arch look on iPhone, the edit bar no longer mentions an Esc key.
Keyboard: in Settings, the left and right arrow keys switch tabs.
Watch together on phones: the mini player no longer covers the newest messages.
Desktop app: in the Apple skin's dark mode, buttons, fields and switches in Settings are visible again.
Desktop app: the Personal space passcode dialog puts Unlock / Encrypt before Cancel, like every other dialog.
Desktop app: search results show a short date and time ("Oct 6, 7:19 PM") that no longer runs over the author's name.
The list of people that pops up when you type @ keeps its "People" heading when you move through it with the arrow keys.
Screen readers: moving through the quick switcher (Ctrl/⌘+K) and the @-mention and emoji suggestions reads out the picked row.
The Get Yap page: the iPhone steps are no longer greyed out.
What's new: the "where to find it" line under each highlight no longer looks like a link.
When's good: on next week, the clear button says "Clear next week".
Windows 98 skin: a doodle reaction opened big has its title bar at the top, like every other window.
Windows 98 skin on phones: the "Sign out" buttons in Your devices no longer break onto two lines.
On phones, small text links like "Cancel", "Let in" and "Show all" are easier to tap.
Windows 98 skin on phones: the invite links in Settings line up the same way on every row.
Draw on phones: the layer chips in the palette are bigger, easier to tap and show what's on each layer.
Apple on phones: drawings you open in Space's Gallery show bigger.
Keyboard: in a call, the Share/Sounds/Leave buttons and Mute/Deafen keep the keyboard focus (it used to vanish every couple of seconds).
Desktop app: pinned messages, search results, Catch up, reply quotes and notifications show plain words instead of **formatting marks**.
Desktop app: the sign-on window uses the same words as the web, and its hint changes with I'm new / I have an account.
Desktop app: the Ping, Delete and Archive questions use the same words as the web.
Desktop app: People asks before resetting someone's PIN, like the web.
Desktop app: turning off an invite link and signing out your other devices ask first, like the web.
Desktop app: in the Apple skin's dark mode, the buttons under someone in People are visible.
Desktop app: when a search in one channel finds nothing, a Search everywhere link tries the whole server.
Desktop app: the sign-on, Set a PIN and custom emoji dialogs start with the cursor in the first field, and Enter finishes them.
Desktop app: the update window shows every note in full, with a friendlier date, and never says you're up to date before it has checked.
Desktop app: in People, an away message says which day the person is back ("back tomorrow, 9:00 AM").
iPhone and Mac: in the Windows 98 look, radio buttons have their full sunken edge, so the dark scheme's ones are easy to see.
iPhone and Mac: in the Apple look, the "Jump to first unread" button is easy to read over messages.
iPhone and Mac: with large text, Settings buttons wrap instead of being cut off.
iPhone and Mac: in the Apple look with very large text, Mute and Deafen match and the call's Leave button stays whole.
iPhone and Mac: VoiceOver reads the Mac's Windows 98 title-bar buttons by name, and says "1 mention".
iPhone and Mac: in the Windows 98 look on a sideways iPhone, the blue title bar reaches both edges.
Desktop app: long channel names and long names in a voice channel end in "…" instead of being cut off or running under the icons.
Desktop app: Windows 98's voice panel is tidier: just the channel name under "Voice connected" (the numbers are still in the status bar).
iPhone and Mac: in the Arch look on a sideways iPhone, sheets' borders line up with their title bars.
iPhone and Mac: in the Apple look, every away-message suggestion is visible.
iPhone and Mac: on the Mac, the Apple look's window can be made small again while a sign-in alert shows.
Desktop app: when you move around with Tab, the button, box or option that has the focus is marked (Windows 98's dotted box, a ring in Apple and Arch).
Desktop app: the Add a sound window no longer splits "(≤ 5 s)" over two lines.
Desktop app: in the Apple skin, Turn away and Later on the waiting-room and PIN bars look like buttons again in light mode.
Desktop app: in the Windows 98 skin, a message that starts with a quote no longer has a grey bar over the sender's name.
Desktop app: in a channel with a long name, the empty message box no longer grows to two lines in a narrow window.
Desktop app: the search panel's tips line wraps neatly in a narrow window.
Desktop app: when it can't reach the server, the app says why in plain words instead of an error code.
Desktop app: in the Arch skin, unread channels are bold with a "*" and read ones are dimmed, like the web (no more extra bar and square).
iPhone and Mac: ⇧⌘F searches messages from anywhere, like on the web.
Desktop app: in the Windows 98 skin, the people on Draw or Space are greyed so they don't look like more places.
Desktop app: in the Apple skin's light mode, green words like "Voice connected" are easier to read.
Desktop app: the reply bar and search results cut long text at a word, with a single "…".
Desktop app: the waiting room tells you everyone got a ping and that it opens by itself, like the web.
iPhone and Mac: the waiting room uses the same friendly words as the web.
iPhone and Mac: the away-message note in Settings explains who sees it, the same way in every look.
Desktop app: in a narrow window, the yellow bars over the chat (new sign-in, weak PIN, a hang starting) wrap their words instead of hiding them under the buttons.
Desktop app: signing in with a password, the hint talks about your password; after a wrong PIN it says the owner or a mod can reset it.
iPhone and Mac: after a wrong PIN, sign-on says the owner or a mod can reset it.
iPhone and Mac: the sign-on hint mentions a password when you choose one.
iPhone and Mac: in the Windows 98 look, the small grey hints in Settings and on your card are easier to read.
iPhone and Mac: jumping to a message further up (a search result, a pin, a reply's quote) scrolls there again, even when it's above a poll or dice.
iPhone and Mac: an away message ends the same ways as on the web and desktop: until your next message, 1 hour, 3 hours or tomorrow morning.

releases.title: Smoother voice and a big polish pass
items: Settings no longer turns your microphone on; use Test mic in Settings › Voice to see your level.
Settings no longer jumps around when you switch tabs.
When Yap can't reach the server at launch it says so, with Try again.
Long channel names and notes no longer run under the header buttons on narrow windows.
Search, Pinned and Pictures now open on narrow windows too (floating over the chat).
The voice panel's quality picker reads "Own quality" / "128k for everyone", like the web.
Lots of join requests collapse into one bar with Review.
Screen sharing now sends the shared tab's sound in stereo and in higher quality.
Voice calls use less data, especially on shaky connections.
Settings tabs are in the same order as on the web; Join & mute sounds moved to Voice.
Wording matches the web app (Yap Properties, Theme, Color…), and Settings' tabs fit in the Apple skin.
Signing out asks first, and Draw's Clear buttons no longer look like the safe choice.
The mic meter's mark and the reaction picker's size.
Voice activation no longer clips the start of what you say, and holds on a little longer at the end of sentences.
Push-to-talk keeps sending for a moment after you let go, so your last word isn't cut off.
A noisy room (fan, computer hum) no longer keeps your mic open in voice activity mode.
Settings › Voice › Hide my IP address in calls (when the server has a voice relay).
Screen sharing works in the browser now. Before, pressing Share quietly did nothing.
If your microphone is unplugged, swapped or switched by your computer during a call, Yap picks it back up by itself.
Yap tells you when your mic is sending pure silence (like a mute switch on the headset).
An old backup can't bring deleted posts back.
Deleted pictures leave the backups; a restore brings back only what's used.
Turning pushes off now stays off. Before, they could quietly come back on the next time Yap reconnected.
iPhone/Mac: being signed out from another device now fully signs this one out (it no longer rejoins voice or keeps the Personal space unlocked).
Mentions are exact: "@Sam Lee" only notifies Sam Lee (not Sam too), and @names inside code or links don't notify anyone.
iPhone/Mac: invites are personal links for everyone; the main invite link is for the owner and mods, with a warning.
iPhone/Mac: Ping everyone always asks first (with an optional message).
iPhone (Apple skin): no more second search box under the message field; search is the magnifier at the top.
Arch sheets keep their border down to the screen's edge.

releases.title: Thirteen extras
items: Draw and Space open signed in, straight to the place
Extras — polls, server-rolled dice, soundboard + chimes, away messages, quiet hours, hang reminders, doodle reactions, media shelf, catch-up counts, save to Personal
Spoilers — wrap text in ||double bars|| and it stays hidden until someone clicks it.
Polls — type /poll Question? | option | option; everyone votes with one click.
/roll and /flip — dice and coin flips rolled by the server, so nobody can fake a nat 20.
Doodle reactions — draw a tiny wiggly pixel doodle and stick it on any message.
Soundboard — short clips anyone in voice can play for the channel, with a volume cap so nothing blasts.
Join chimes — pick the sound everyone hears when you join their voice channel (or upload your own).
Away messages — like AIM: set one, and people who mention you get it as a quiet reply.
Quiet hours — no pushes at night, or snooze them until tomorrow morning.
Hang reminders — plan a time from When's good; whoever's free gets one reminder when it starts.
Catch up — one list of what's new in the channels you haven't read, plus a 'New since' line.
Pictures & GIFs shelf — every picture in a channel as a grid.
Save to Personal — bookmark any message into your Personal space.
Quick switcher — Ctrl/⌘+K to jump to any channel, place or person.
YouTube links get a 'Watch together' button.
The privacy page now covers poll votes, soundboard clips, away messages, hangs and quiet hours.

Space: walk into the campfire and you're on fire, splash in water and you drip; a Music room with a floor piano and drums, a Pond, a race track, water balloons (F) and timed laps.
Tell the voice track from a screen share by transceiver, not stream id

Space doesn't go blank if your connection hiccups.

items: A small native desktop app for Windows and Linux (and Mac) with push-to-talk that works even while you're in a game.

@mention people to ping them — mentions are highlighted and counted in the sidebar.

Nightly backups of everything.

items: Text channels and voice channels. That's it.

highlights.title: Links to every place
highlights.text: Draw, Space, Watch, When's good, the board and every text channel have their own link. Copy it (the link button by the name on the web; right-click or long-press in the apps) and send it: anyone here who opens it lands right there.

highlights.title: Safer sign-ins
highlights.text: Choosing a new password signs out your other devices (an owner or mod's reset signs out all of yours), a sign-in link opened in a browser asks whose account it signed you in to, and nobody can take a name that looks just like yours.

highlights.title: Nothing a friend sends can crash your app
highlights.text: Odd pictures, GIFs, sound clips and call data can't crash or freeze the desktop, iPhone or Mac app any more, and Hide my IP never falls back to a direct connection.

highlights.title: OBS: everyone, or everyone but you
highlights.text: A Stream to OBS link plays everyone in the call, your own voice too, from whichever device you're on: talk on your phone and record the game on your PC. Or pick Everyone but you. New links don't contain the invite link.

highlights.title: Drafts, new messages and Rejoin
highlights.text: What you type stays with its channel when you switch. A "↓ New messages" pill shows when someone writes while you're scrolled up. After a reload or a crash, a bar offers to put you back in the call you were in. And Settings › Voice has a Mic volume slider.

highlights.title: Steadier everywhere
highlights.text: Dropped connections are noticed in seconds, a message sent just as the connection dropped no longer shows up twice, the desktop app can't crash on odd invite links or emoji, and the iPhone app stops interrupting your music after a call. Pushes about a message now open that message.

highlights.title: A new Yap icon
highlights.text: A cleaner pixel speech bubble on teal. It shows on the web and in browser tabs right away, and on the iPhone, Mac and desktop apps with their next update. On iPhone it follows dark and tinted Home Screens too.

highlights.title: A simpler Yap icon
highlights.text: Yap has one icon everywhere now: the little pixel speech bubble on teal. It shows on the web and in browser tabs right away, and on the iPhone, Mac and desktop apps with their next update.

highlights.title: A polish pass everywhere
highlights.text: Over a hundred small fixes across the web, desktop and iPhone/Mac apps: every button reachable with the keyboard and screen readers, tidier phone layouts in all three skins, the same plain words in every app, and on iPhone, jumping to an older message scrolls there again.

highlights.title: Calls ride out hiccups
highlights.text: A Wi-Fi blip or a Yap update no longer cuts your call: no gap, no burst of leave/join chimes. Someone whose connection drops for a moment shows as "reconnecting…" instead of leaving. Works on the web, the desktop app and the iPhone/Mac app.

highlights.title: Your first word gets through
highlights.text: Voice activity opens just before you start talking instead of clipping your first syllable, ignores a steady fan, and keeps word endings. Settings › Voice › Hear yourself plays back how you sound to others.

highlights.title: Layers in Draw
highlights.text: Draw has three layers: sketch on the bottom one, colour in the middle and ink on top, and the eraser only touches the layer you're on. Hide a layer just for you with its eye; Save, GIF and Share give you what you see.

highlights.title: Soundboard and join chimes
highlights.text: Play short clips for everyone in your voice channel, and pick the sound people hear when you join (or upload your own). Loud clips are turned down for everyone, and your own soundboard volume and mute switch are in Settings › Voice.

highlights.title: Polls, dice and spoilers
highlights.text: /poll Question? | A | B makes a poll anyone can vote in. /roll and /flip are rolled by the server, so nobody can fake a nat 20. Wrap text in ||double bars|| to hide a spoiler.

highlights.title: Doodle reactions
highlights.text: Draw a tiny wiggly pixel doodle and stick it on a message, like WigglyPaint in a reaction.

highlights.title: Away messages (like AIM)
highlights.text: Set one in Settings › Profile. Anyone who mentions you gets it as a quiet reply; it ends by itself when you're back.

highlights.title: Hang reminders and quiet hours
highlights.text: Pick a time in When's good and plan a hang: whoever's free gets one reminder when it starts. Quiet hours keep pushes away at night, or snooze them until morning.

highlights.title: Catch up, quick switcher, media shelf
highlights.text: See what's new in the channels you missed in one list, jump anywhere with Ctrl/⌘+K, and browse every picture and GIF in a channel. Bookmark any message into your Personal space.

highlights.title: Watch together
highlights.text: Paste a YouTube link and everyone watches the same moment, with theater seats, your own volume and a queue. It keeps playing in a mini player while you chat, and voice stays on.

highlights.title: Screen sharing, up to 1080p 60 fps (or 4K)
highlights.text: Share a window, your whole screen or a tab with your voice channel; friends click LIVE to watch, or pop it out while they chat.

highlights.title: Space got big
highlights.text: Eight rooms that are their own voice zones, football, tag, water balloons, timed race laps, a floor piano, and yes: walk into the campfire and you're on fire.

highlights.title: The desktop app
highlights.text: A real app for Windows, Linux and Mac (no Electron): push-to-talk that works in games, Draw and Space built in, and one-click updates.

highlights.title: An encrypted Personal space
highlights.text: Notes to yourself, locked with a passcode only you know; not even the server can read them.

highlights.title: Search and pins
highlights.text: Find any message (from:Name, has:image) and pin the good ones to a channel.

highlights.title: Three looks
highlights.text: Windows 98 / AIM, a clean Apple-style skin, and a terminal-y Arch skin with IRC-style chat.

highlights.title: Replies and long messages
highlights.text: Reply to a specific message (it pings them), and messages can be up to 40,000 characters.

highlights.title: Chill mode
highlights.text: No online/offline lights or member list watching you; deleted posts are really erased.
highlights.where: People button for the member list

highlights.title: Pixel-art Draw with GIFs
highlights.text: Wobbly WigglyPaint-style lines; save the page as an animated GIF.
